name: Resource Requirements
purpose: Describes the type and quantity of resources needed to complete the project work: people, equipment, material, supplies and, as needed, locations such as training rooms or testing sites. The requirements follow the project scope, so they stay stable while scope is stable, evolve when scope evolves, and become more detailed and more stable over time.

elements.guidance: Whether the resource is a team resource or a physical one; if physical, whether equipment, supplies, material, location or another kind.
The number or quantity needed for the activity, with the unit of measure used.
Assumptions about the resource, such as availability or certifications.
Basis of estimate, grade, competency or other relevant information.

tailoring: Divide the form into two sections, one for team resources and one for physical resources, or one for internal resources and one for contracted or purchased resources.
Consider a basis of estimates column with the estimating method for quantities, the range of estimates, the confidence level, and constraints or risks tied to the resource.
For projects with large amounts of inventory, supplies or material, document support requirements such as inventory, supply chain and logistics.

notes: The sources list prints 'Cost estimates resource calendars' as one bullet (no comma); it is recorded as printed, and whether it means cost estimates (2.20) plus resource calendars is not stated in the book. 2.20 says it provides to Resource requirements while 2.28 lists cost estimates as a source, so the two forms feed each other.
